source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Hebrew titles are translated inside public verse 1. Separate title records in Psalms 3–9, 12–13, and 18–22 bind jointly with Hebrew verse 2 to public verse 1; subsequent public labels are offset by one. Psalm 13 public verses 5 and 6 partition Hebrew 13:6 at direct-child word boundaries 1–6 and 7–11. Both retain the full original record hash and its numbering notes. Other labels match. All 325 original source records are covered; one is explicitly partitioned across two public verses.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Preserves walking-standing-sitting progression and inclusive human referent.
verses.before: Blessed is the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand in the path of sinners, nor sit in the seat of scoffers;
verses.after: Happy is the person who does not walk by the counsel of the wicked, stand in the path of sinners, or sit among scoffers,
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed is the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand in the path of sinners, nor sit in the seat of scoffers;

verses.rationale: Retains vocal meditation and recurring instruction term.
verses.before: but his delight is in the law of the LORD, and on his law he meditates day and night.
verses.after: but delights in the LORD’s instruction and murmurs it over day and night.
verses.tsw_comparator: but his delight is in the law of the LORD, and on his law he meditates day and night.

verses.rationale: Keeps planted tree, seasons, and flourishing image.
verses.before: He is like a tree planted by streams of water, which yields its fruit in its season, and its leaf does not wither— in all that he does, he prospers.
verses.after: That person is like a tree planted beside streams of water, bearing fruit in season, its leaves never withering. Whatever that person does flourishes.
verses.tsw_comparator: He is like a tree planted by streams of water, which yields its fruit in its season, and its leaf does not wither— in all that he does, he prospers.

verses.rationale: Preserves sharp contrast and weightless agricultural image.
verses.before: Not so the wicked! They are like chaff that the wind drives away.
verses.after: The wicked are not like this; they are chaff the wind drives away.
verses.tsw_comparator: Not so the wicked! They are like chaff that the wind drives away.

verses.rationale: Keeps standing echo and communal judgment.
verses.before: So the wicked will not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous;
verses.after: So the wicked will not stand in judgment, nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore the wicked will not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous;

verses.rationale: Retains relational knowing and two ways.
verses.before: for the LORD knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked will perish.
verses.after: For the LORD knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked comes to ruin.
verses.tsw_comparator: for the LORD knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked will perish.

verses.rationale: Keeps turmoil and vain deliberation echoing meditation.
verses.before: Why do the nations rage and the peoples plot in vain?
verses.after: Why do the nations rage and the peoples plot emptiness?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why do the nations rage and the peoples plot in vain?

verses.rationale: Preserves royal opposition and anointed title.
verses.before: The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the LORD and against his anointed, saying,
verses.after: The kings of the earth take their stand; rulers gather together against the LORD and his anointed one:
verses.tsw_comparator: The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the LORD and against his anointed, saying,

verses.rationale: Marks rebellious rulers’ direct speech.
verses.before: “Let us burst their bonds apart and cast away their cords from us.”
verses.after: “Let us tear apart their bonds and throw their cords off us!”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Let us burst their bonds apart and cast away their cords from us.”

verses.rationale: Retains divine laughter and Adonai distinction.
verses.before: He who sits in the heavens laughs; the Lord holds them in derision.
verses.after: The one enthroned in heaven laughs; the Lord holds them in derision.
verses.tsw_comparator: He who sits in the heavens laughs; the Lord holds them in derision.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine anger without softening.
verses.before: Then he will speak to them in his wrath, and terrify them in his fury, saying,
verses.after: Then he speaks to them in anger and terrifies them in his fury:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he will speak to them in his wrath, and terrify them in his fury, saying,

verses.rationale: Makes divine king-installing voice explicit.
verses.before: “As for me, I have set my King on Zion, my holy hill.”
verses.after: “I myself have installed my king on Zion, my holy mountain.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “As for me, I have set my King on Zion, my holy hill.”

verses.rationale: Preserves royal speaker and begetting language.
verses.before: I will tell of the decree: The LORD said to me, “You are my Son; today I have begotten you.
verses.after: I will declare the decree: the LORD said to me, “You are my son; today I have begotten you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will tell of the decree: The LORD said to me, “You are my Son; today I have begotten you.

verses.rationale: Keeps expansive inheritance promise.
verses.before: Ask of me, and I will make the nations your heritage, and the ends of the earth your possession.
verses.after: Ask of me, and I will give you nations as your inheritance, the ends of the earth as your possession.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ask of me, and I will make the nations your heritage, and the ends of the earth your possession.

verses.rationale: Follows pointed break reading and violent pottery image.
verses.before: You will break them with a rod of iron and dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.”
verses.after: You will break them with an iron rod, shatter them like a potter’s vessel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall break them with a rod of iron and dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.”

verses.rationale: Retains admonition to political rulers.
verses.before: Now therefore, O kings, be wise; be warned, O rulers of the earth.
verses.after: Now, kings, be wise; rulers of the earth, accept correction.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now therefore, O kings, be wise; be warned, O rulers of the earth.

verses.rationale: Keeps joy and fear together.
verses.before: Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling.
verses.after: Serve the LORD with reverence; rejoice with trembling.
verses.tsw_comparator: Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling.

verses.rationale: Retains difficult kiss-son reading with alternatives in note.
verses.before: Kiss the Son, lest he be angry, and you perish in the way, for his wrath is quickly kindled. Blessed are everyone who take refuge in him.
verses.after: Kiss the son, lest he grow angry and you perish on the way, for his anger can flare in a moment. Happy are all who take refuge in him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Kiss the Son, lest he be angry, and you perish in the way, for his wrath is quickly kindled. Blessed are all who take refuge in him.

verses.rationale: Binds separate Hebrew title and first prayer in public verse1.
verses.before: O LORD, how many are my foes! Many are rising against me;
verses.after: A psalm of David, when he fled from his son Absalom. LORD, how many are my foes! So many rise against me.
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, how many are my foes! Many are rising against me;

verses.rationale: Preserves enemies’ denial and unexpanded Selah.
verses.before: many are saying of my soul, “There is no salvation for him in God.” Selah.
verses.after: So many say of me, “There is no rescue for him in God.” Selah
verses.tsw_comparator: many are saying of my soul, “There is no salvation for him in God.” Selah.

verses.rationale: Keeps protective shield and restored posture.
verses.before: But you, O LORD, are a shield about me, my glory, and the lifter of my head.
verses.after: But you, LORD, are a shield around me, my glory, the one who lifts my head.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you, O LORD, are a shield about me, my glory, and the lifter of my head.

verses.rationale: Retains voice, answer, and mountain connection.
verses.before: I cried aloud to the LORD, and he answered me from his holy hill. Selah.
verses.after: I cry aloud to the LORD, and he answers me from his holy mountain. Selah
verses.tsw_comparator: I cried aloud to the LORD, and he answered me from his holy hill. Selah.

verses.rationale: Makes sleep-and-waking trust concrete.
verses.before: I lay down and slept; I woke again, for the LORD sustained me.
verses.after: I lay down and slept; I woke again, because the LORD sustained me.
verses.tsw_comparator: I lay down and slept; I woke again, for the LORD sustained me.

verses.rationale: Keeps immense number and encirclement.
verses.before: I will not be afraid of many thousands of people who have set themselves against me all around.
verses.after: I will not fear tens of thousands arrayed against me on every side.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will not be afraid of many thousands of people who have set themselves against me all around.

verses.rationale: Preserves violent appeal and completed/confident action.
verses.before: Arise, O LORD! Save me, O my God! For you strike all my enemies on the cheek; you break the teeth of the wicked.
verses.after: Rise, LORD! Save me, my God! You strike all my enemies on the cheek; you break the teeth of the wicked.
verses.tsw_comparator: Arise, O LORD! Save me, O my God! For you strike all my enemies on the cheek; you break the teeth of the wicked.

verses.rationale: Moves from individual prayer to people’s blessing.
verses.before: Salvation belongs to the LORD; your blessing be upon your people! Selah.
verses.after: Rescue belongs to the LORD. May your blessing rest on your people. Selah
verses.tsw_comparator: Salvation belongs to the LORD; your blessing be upon your people! Selah.

verses.rationale: Retains source title and distress-to-room image.
verses.before: Answer me when I call, O God of my righteousness! You have given me relief when I was in distress; be gracious to me and hear my prayer!
verses.after: For the director. With stringed instruments. A psalm of David. Answer when I call, God who vindicates me! You gave me room when I was hemmed in. Be gracious to me and hear my prayer.
verses.tsw_comparator: Answer me when I call, O God of my righteousness! You have given me relief when I was in distress; be gracious to me and hear my prayer!

verses.rationale: Reads sons-of-man as socially weighty opponents.
verses.before: O sons of men, how long will my honor be turned into shame? How long will you love vain words and seek after lies? Selah.
verses.after: You men of standing, how long will you turn my honor to shame, love emptiness, and chase a lie? Selah
verses.tsw_comparator: O sons of men, how long shall my honor be turned into shame? How long will you love vain words and seek after lies? Selah.

verses.rationale: Preserves faithful person and responsive hearing.
verses.before: But know that the LORD has set apart the faithful for himself; the LORD hears when I call to him.
verses.after: Know that the LORD has set apart the faithful for himself; the LORD hears when I call to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: But know that the LORD has set apart the faithful for himself; the LORD hears when I call to him.

verses.rationale: Follows tremble sense with anger alternative noted.
verses.before: Be angry, and do not sin; ponder in your own hearts on your beds, and be silent. Selah.
verses.after: Tremble, and do not sin; speak within your hearts on your beds, and be still. Selah
verses.tsw_comparator: Be angry, and do not sin; ponder in your own hearts on your beds, and be silent. Selah.

verses.rationale: Keeps worship and trust paired.
verses.before: Offer right sacrifices, and put your trust in the LORD.
verses.after: Offer righteous sacrifices and put your trust in the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Offer right sacrifices, and put your trust in the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves quoted question and face-light appeal.
verses.before: There are many who say, “Who will show us some good?” Lift up the light of your face upon us, O LORD!
verses.after: Many ask, “Who will show us good?” Let the light of your face shine on us, LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: There are many who say, “Who will show us some good?” Lift up the light of your face upon us, O LORD!

verses.rationale: Retains comparative joy and harvest wealth.
verses.before: You have put more joy in my heart than they have when their grain and wine abound.
verses.after: You have put joy in my heart, more than when their grain and new wine abound.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have put more joy in my heart than they have when their grain and wine abound.

verses.rationale: Keeps sleep, exclusivity, and secure dwelling.
verses.before: In peace I will both lie down and sleep; for you alone, O LORD, make me dwell in safety.
verses.after: In peace I will lie down and sleep, for you alone, LORD, let me live in safety.
verses.tsw_comparator: In peace I will both lie down and sleep; for you alone, O LORD, make me dwell in safety.

verses.rationale: Retains uncertain performance term rather than guessing instrument.
verses.before: Give ear to my words, O LORD; consider my groaning.
verses.after: For the director. For the Nehiloth. A psalm of David. Listen to my words, LORD; attend to my murmuring.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give ear to my words, O LORD; consider my groaning.

verses.rationale: Keeps personal royal and divine addresses.
verses.before: Give attention to the sound of my cry, my King and my God, for to you do I pray.
verses.after: Hear my cry for help, my King and my God, for it is to you that I pray.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give attention to the sound of my cry, my King and my God, for to you do I pray.

verses.rationale: Retains morning repetition and expectant watching.
verses.before: O LORD, in the morning you hear my voice; in the morning I prepare a sacrifice for you and watch.
verses.after: LORD, in the morning you hear my voice; in the morning I lay my prayer before you and watch.
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, in the morning you hear my voice; in the morning I prepare a sacrifice for you and watch.

verses.rationale: Keeps evil as unwelcome guest.
verses.before: For you are not a God who delights in wickedness; evil may not dwell with you.
verses.after: You are no God who delights in wickedness; evil cannot lodge with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you are not a God who delights in wickedness; evil may not dwell with you.

verses.rationale: Retains force of hatred rather than depersonalizing object.
verses.before: The boastful will not stand before your eyes; you hate all evildoers.
verses.after: The boastful cannot stand before your eyes; you hate everyone who does wrong.
verses.tsw_comparator: The boastful shall not stand before your eyes; you hate all evildoers.

verses.rationale: Preserves destruction and actual violence.
verses.before: You destroy people who speak lies; the LORD abhors the bloodthirsty and deceitful man.
verses.after: You destroy those who tell lies; the LORD abhors the bloodthirsty and deceitful.
verses.tsw_comparator: You destroy those who speak lies; the LORD abhors the bloodthirsty and deceitful man.

verses.rationale: Keeps covenantal love and direction of worship.
verses.before: Yet I, through the abundance of your steadfast love, will enter your house. I will bow down toward your holy temple in the fear of you.
verses.after: But through your abundant faithful love I enter your house; in reverence I bow toward your holy temple.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I, through the abundance of your steadfast love, will enter your house. I will bow down toward your holy temple in the fear of you.

verses.rationale: Follows read straighten imperative and divine way.
verses.before: Lead me, O LORD, in your righteousness because of my enemies; make your way straight before me.
verses.after: LORD, lead me in your righteousness because of my enemies; make your way straight before me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Lead me, O LORD, in your righteousness because of my enemies; make your way straight before me.

verses.rationale: Preserves bodily sequence and dangerous flattery.
verses.before: For there is no truth in their mouth; their inner being is destruction; their throat is an open grave; they flatter with their tongue.
verses.after: Nothing in their mouths is reliable; within them is destruction. Their throats are open graves; their tongues speak smoothly.
verses.tsw_comparator: For there is no truth in their mouth; their inner being is destruction; their throat is an open grave; they flatter with their tongue.

verses.rationale: Keeps imprecation, self-defeating plans, and stated reason.
verses.before: Make them bear their guilt, O God; let them fall by their own counsels; because of the abundance of their transgressions cast them out, for they have rebelled against you.
verses.after: Declare them guilty, God! Let their own schemes bring them down. Drive them out for their many rebellions, for they have rebelled against you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Make them bear their guilt, O God; let them fall by their own counsels; because of the abundance of their transgressions cast them out, for they have rebelled against you.

verses.rationale: Retains refuge, shelter, and communal song.
verses.before: But let everyone who take refuge in you rejoice; let them ever sing for joy, and spread your protection over them, that people who love your name may exult in you.
verses.after: Let all who take refuge in you rejoice; let them sing for joy forever. Spread your shelter over them, so those who love your name may exult in you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But let all who take refuge in you rejoice; let them ever sing for joy, and spread your protection over them, that those who love your name may exult in you.

verses.rationale: Keeps favor’s encircling shield image.
verses.before: For you bless the righteous, O LORD; you cover him with favor as with a shield.
verses.after: For you bless the righteous, LORD; you surround them with favor like a shield.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you bless the righteous, O LORD; you cover him with favor as with a shield.

verses.rationale: Preserves uncertain title term and restrained rebuke plea.
verses.before: O LORD, do not rebuke me in your anger, nor discipline me in your wrath.
verses.after: For the director. With stringed instruments, according to the Sheminith. A psalm of David. LORD, do not rebuke me in your anger or correct me in your fury.
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, do not rebuke me in your anger, nor discipline me in your wrath.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated name and bodily terror.
verses.before: Be gracious to me, O LORD, for I am weak; heal me, O LORD, for my bones are troubled.
verses.after: Be gracious to me, LORD, for I am wasting away. Heal me, LORD, for my bones are terrified.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be gracious to me, O LORD, for I am weak; heal me, O LORD, for my bones are troubled.

verses.rationale: Retains abrupt unfinished address and repeated terror.
verses.before: My soul also is greatly troubled. But you, O LORD—how long?
verses.after: My whole being is deeply terrified. And you, LORD—how long?
verses.tsw_comparator: My soul also is greatly troubled. But you, O LORD—how long?

verses.rationale: Keeps divine turning and loyal-love appeal.
verses.before: Turn, O LORD, deliver my life; save me for the sake of your steadfast love.
verses.after: Turn back, LORD; rescue my life. Save me for the sake of your faithful love.
verses.tsw_comparator: Turn, O LORD, deliver my life; save me for the sake of your steadfast love.

verses.rationale: Preserves lament’s claim without doctrinal correction.
verses.before: For in death there is no remembrance of you; in Sheol who will give you praise?
verses.after: For in death no one remembers you; in Sheol, who gives you thanks?
verses.tsw_comparator: For in death there is no remembrance of you; in Sheol who will give you praise?

verses.rationale: Keeps extravagant tears and nightly exhaustion.
verses.before: I am weary with my groaning; every night I flood my bed with tears; I drench my couch with my weeping.
verses.after: I am worn out with groaning. Every night I flood my bed; my tears drench my couch.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am weary with my groaning; every night I flood my bed with tears; I drench my couch with my weeping.

verses.rationale: Retains bodily aging caused by distress.
verses.before: My eye wastes away because of grief; it grows weak because of all my foes.
verses.after: My eyes waste away with grief; they grow old because of all my foes.
verses.tsw_comparator: My eye wastes away because of grief; it grows weak because of all my foes.

verses.rationale: Makes confident turn audible while retaining tears.
verses.before: Depart from me, all you workers of evil, for the LORD has heard the sound of my weeping.
verses.after: Away from me, all who do wrong! The LORD has heard the sound of my weeping.
verses.tsw_comparator: Depart from me, all you workers of evil, for the LORD has heard the sound of my weeping.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated divine hearing and receiving.
verses.before: The LORD has heard my plea; the LORD accepts my prayer.
verses.after: The LORD has heard my plea; the LORD receives my prayer.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has heard my plea; the LORD accepts my prayer.

verses.rationale: Carries terror from sufferer to enemies.
verses.before: All my enemies will be ashamed and greatly troubled; they will turn back and be put to shame in a moment.
verses.after: All my enemies will be shamed and deeply terrified; they will turn back, suddenly put to shame.
verses.tsw_comparator: All my enemies shall be ashamed and greatly troubled; they shall turn back and be put to shame in a moment.

verses.rationale: Retains uncertain genre title and named setting.
verses.before: O LORD my God, in you I take refuge; save me from all my pursuers and deliver me,
verses.after: A Shiggaion of David, which he sang to the LORD concerning Cush, a Benjaminite. LORD my God, I take refuge in you. Save me from all who pursue me; deliver me,
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD my God, in you I take refuge; save me from all my pursuers and deliver me,

verses.rationale: Keeps predation and absent deliverer.
verses.before: lest like a lion they tear my soul apart, rending it in pieces, with none to rescue.
verses.after: lest an enemy tear me apart like a lion, ripping me to pieces with no one to rescue me.
verses.tsw_comparator: lest like a lion they tear my soul apart, rending it in pieces, with none to rescue.

verses.rationale: Preserves conditional oath, not confession.
verses.before: O LORD my God, if I have done this, if there is wrong in my hands,
verses.after: LORD my God, if I have done this, if injustice is on my hands,
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD my God, if I have done this, if there is wrong in my hands,

verses.rationale: Selects rescue reading; plunder alternative explicitly noted.
verses.before: if I have repaid my friend with evil or plundered my enemy without cause,
verses.after: if I repaid a peaceful ally with evil— I even rescued one who opposed me without cause—
verses.tsw_comparator: if I have repaid my friend with evil or plundered my enemy without cause,

verses.rationale: Retains self-curse and grounded honor.
verses.before: let the enemy pursue my soul and overtake it, and let him trample my life to the ground and lay my glory in the dust. Selah.
verses.after: then let an enemy pursue and overtake me, trample my life into the ground, and lay my honor in the dust. Selah
verses.tsw_comparator: let the enemy pursue my soul and overtake it, and let him trample my life to the ground and lay my glory in the dust. Selah.

verses.rationale: Preserves anger against anger and judicial appeal.
verses.before: Arise, O LORD, in your anger; lift yourself up against the fury of my enemies; awake for me—you have appointed a judgment.
verses.after: Rise in anger, LORD; stand against my enemies’ fury. Awake for me; you have commanded justice.
verses.tsw_comparator: Arise, O LORD, in your anger; lift yourself up against the fury of my enemies; awake for me—you have appointed a judgment.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine high seat and gathered peoples.
verses.before: Let the assembly of the peoples be gathered about you; over it return on high.
verses.after: Let the assembly of peoples surround you; return to your high place above them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the assembly of the peoples be gathered about you; over it return on high.

verses.rationale: Retains personal claim of right and integrity.
verses.before: The LORD judges the peoples; judge me, O LORD, according to my righteousness and according to the integrity that is in me.
verses.after: The LORD judges the peoples. Judge me, LORD, according to my righteousness, according to the integrity within me.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD judges the peoples; judge me, O LORD, according to my righteousness and according to the integrity that is in me.

verses.rationale: Preserves ancient organs with vocabulary explanation.
verses.before: Oh, let the evil of the wicked come to an end, and may you establish the righteous— you who test the minds and hearts, O righteous God!
verses.after: Bring the evil of the wicked to an end and establish the righteous, you righteous God who tests hearts and kidneys.
verses.tsw_comparator: Oh, let the evil of the wicked come to an end, and may you establish the righteous— you who test the minds and hearts, O righteous God!

verses.rationale: Keeps protection’s location and upright heart.
verses.before: My shield is with God, who saves the upright in heart.
verses.after: My shield is with God, who saves the upright in heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: My shield is with God, who saves the upright in heart.

verses.rationale: Preserves sustained indignation without adding object.
verses.before: God is a righteous judge, and a God who feels indignation every day.
verses.after: God is a righteous judge, a God who expresses indignation every day.
verses.tsw_comparator: God is a righteous judge, and a God who feels indignation every day.

verses.rationale: Clarifies shifting agents; alternative subject noted.
verses.before: If one does not repent, God will sharpen his sword; he has bent and readied his bow;
verses.after: If a person does not turn back, God sharpens his sword; he bends his bow and makes it ready.
verses.tsw_comparator: If one does not repent, God will sharpen his sword; he has bent and readied his bow;

verses.rationale: Retains actual weapons and fire.
verses.before: he has prepared for him his deadly weapons, making his arrows fiery shafts.
verses.after: He prepares deadly weapons and makes his arrows burn.
verses.tsw_comparator: he has prepared for him his deadly weapons, making his arrows fiery shafts.

verses.rationale: Keeps pregnancy sequence for generated harm.
verses.before: Look, the wicked conceives evil and is pregnant with mischief and gives birth to lies.
verses.after: See how the wicked labor with wrongdoing, conceive trouble, and give birth to falsehood.
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, the wicked conceives evil and is pregnant with mischief and gives birth to lies.

verses.rationale: Retains self-entrapment, inclusive collective wicked.
verses.before: He makes a pit, digging it out, and falls into the hole that he has made.
verses.after: They dig a pit and deepen it, then fall into the hole they made.
verses.tsw_comparator: He makes a pit, digging it out, and falls into the hole that he has made.

verses.rationale: Preserves paired bodily rebound images.
verses.before: His mischief returns upon his own head, and on his own skull his violence descends.
verses.after: Their trouble returns on their own heads; their violence falls on their own crowns.
verses.tsw_comparator: His mischief returns upon his own head, and on his own skull his violence descends.

verses.rationale: Keeps thanksgiving and divine title.
verses.before: I will give thanks to the LORD according to his righteousness, and I will sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High.
verses.after: I will thank the LORD for his righteousness and sing to the name of the LORD Most High.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will give thanks to the LORD according to his righteousness, and I will sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High.

verses.rationale: Retains title and difficult splendor clause with note.
verses.before: O LORD, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth! You have set your glory above the heavens.
verses.after: For the director. According to the Gittith. A psalm of David. LORD, our Lord, how majestic is your name throughout the earth! You have set your splendor above the heavens.
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth! You have set your glory above the heavens.

verses.rationale: Follows Hebrew strength rather than later praise rendering.
verses.before: Out of the mouths of infants and nursing children you have established strength because of your foes, to silence the enemy and the avenger.
verses.after: From the mouths of children and nursing infants you have established strength against your foes, to silence the enemy and the avenger.
verses.tsw_comparator: Out of the mouths of infants and nursing children you have established strength because of your foes, to silence the enemy and the avenger.

verses.rationale: Retains divine fingers and night-sky observation.
verses.before: When I look at your heavens, the work of your fingers, the moon and the stars that you have set in place,
verses.after: When I see your heavens, the work of your fingers, the moon and stars you have established,
verses.tsw_comparator: When I look at your heavens, the work of your fingers, the moon and the stars that you have set in place,

verses.rationale: Uses inclusive humanity for parallel mortal/son-of-human.
verses.before: what are human beings that you are mindful of them, mortals that you care for them?
verses.after: what are mortals, that you remember them, human beings, that you attend to them?
verses.tsw_comparator: what are human beings that you are mindful of them, mortals that you care for them?

verses.rationale: Selects God sense of elohim; heavenly beings alternative noted.
verses.before: Yet you have made them a little lower than the divine, and crowned them with glory and honor.
verses.after: You made them a little lower than God and crowned them with glory and splendor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet you have made them a little lower than the divine, and crowned them with glory and honor.

verses.rationale: Keeps delegated rule and underfoot image.
verses.before: You have given them dominion over the works of your hands; you have put everything under their feet,
verses.after: You gave them rule over the work of your hands; you placed everything beneath their feet:
verses.tsw_comparator: You have given them dominion over the works of your hands; you have put all things under their feet,

verses.rationale: Preserves domestic and wild animal scope.
verses.before: all sheep and oxen, and also the beasts of the field,
verses.after: all sheep and cattle, and the wild animals too,
verses.tsw_comparator: all sheep and oxen, and also the beasts of the field,

verses.rationale: Keeps sea paths and broad final creature phrase.
verses.before: the birds of the air, and the fish of the sea, whatever passes along the paths of the seas.
verses.after: the birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea, whatever travels the paths of the seas.
verses.tsw_comparator: the birds of the air, and the fish of the sea, whatever passes along the paths of the seas.

verses.rationale: Repeats opening refrain exactly.
verses.before: O LORD, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth!
verses.after: LORD, our Lord, how majestic is your name throughout the earth!
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth!

verses.rationale: Retains uncertain title and total-hearted recounting.
verses.before: I will give thanks to the LORD with my whole heart; I will recount all your wondrous deeds.
verses.after: For the director. According to Muth-labben. A psalm of David. I will thank the LORD with my whole heart; I will recount all your wonders.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will give thanks to the LORD with my whole heart; I will recount all your wondrous deeds.

verses.rationale: Keeps paired joy and named divine title.
verses.before: I will be glad and exult in you; I will sing praise to your name, O Most High.
verses.after: I will rejoice and exult in you; I will sing to your name, Most High.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will be glad and exult in you; I will sing praise to your name, O Most High.

verses.rationale: Preserves retreat and collapse in divine presence.
verses.before: When my enemies turn back, they stumble and perish before you.
verses.after: When my enemies turn back, they stumble and perish before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: When my enemies turn back, they stumble and perish before you.

verses.rationale: Keeps courtroom and throne joined.
verses.before: For you have maintained my just cause; you have sat on the throne, giving righteous judgment.
verses.after: For you have upheld my cause and my right; you sat on the throne, judging justly.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you have maintained my just cause; you have sat on the throne, giving righteous judgment.

verses.rationale: Preserves annihilated remembrance and emphatic duration.
verses.before: You have rebuked the nations; you have made the wicked perish; you have blotted out their name forever and ever.
verses.after: You rebuked nations and destroyed the wicked; you erased their name forever and ever.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have rebuked the nations; you have made the wicked perish; you have blotted out their name forever and ever.

verses.rationale: Clarifies difficult ruins syntax without weakening destruction.
verses.before: The enemy came to an end in everlasting ruins; their cities you rooted out; the very memory of them has perished.
verses.after: The enemy is finished, a ruin forever. You uprooted their cities; even their memory has perished.
verses.tsw_comparator: The enemy came to an end in everlasting ruins; their cities you rooted out; the very memory of them has perished.

verses.rationale: Keeps contrast between ruined enemy and enduring throne.
verses.before: But the LORD sits enthroned forever; he has established his throne for justice,
verses.after: But the LORD is enthroned forever; he has established his throne for judgment.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD sits enthroned forever; he has established his throne for justice,

verses.rationale: Preserves righteousness and equity as related terms.
verses.before: and he judges the world with righteousness; he judges the peoples with uprightness.
verses.after: He judges the world in righteousness and renders judgment on peoples with equity.
verses.tsw_comparator: and he judges the world with righteousness; he judges the peoples with uprightness.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated stronghold and oppressed referent.
verses.before: The LORD is a stronghold for the oppressed, a stronghold in times of trouble.
verses.after: The LORD is a stronghold for the crushed, a stronghold in times of distress.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD is a stronghold for the oppressed, a stronghold in times of trouble.

verses.rationale: Keeps knowing-name and seeking connection.
verses.before: And people who know your name put their trust in you, for you, O LORD, have not forsaken people who seek you.
verses.after: Those who know your name trust in you, for you have not abandoned those who seek you, LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: And those who know your name put their trust in you, for you, O LORD, have not forsaken those who seek you.

verses.rationale: Preserves Zion and outward proclamation.
verses.before: Sing praises to the LORD, who sits enthroned in Zion! Tell among the peoples his deeds!
verses.after: Sing to the LORD, enthroned in Zion; make his deeds known among the peoples.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sing praises to the LORD, who sits enthroned in Zion! Tell among the peoples his deeds!

verses.rationale: Keeps blood accountability and remembered sufferers.
verses.before: For he who avenges blood is mindful of them; he does not forget the cry of the afflicted.
verses.after: For the one who calls bloodshed to account remembers them; he does not forget the cry of the afflicted.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he who avenges blood is mindful of them; he does not forget the cry of the afflicted.

verses.rationale: Retains urgent request and lifted-from-gates image.
verses.before: Be gracious to me, O LORD! See my affliction from people who hate me, O you who lift me up from the gates of death,
verses.after: Be gracious to me, LORD! See what I suffer from those who hate me, you who lift me from death’s gates,
verses.tsw_comparator: Be gracious to me, O LORD! See my affliction from those who hate me, O you who lift me up from the gates of death,

verses.rationale: Preserves contrasting gates and city personification.
verses.before: that I may recount all your praises, that in the gates of the daughter of Zion I may rejoice in your salvation.
verses.after: so I may recount all your praises at the gates of Daughter Zion and rejoice in your rescue.
verses.tsw_comparator: that I may recount all your praises, that in the gates of the daughter of Zion I may rejoice in your salvation.

verses.rationale: Keeps two self-entrapment images.
verses.before: The nations have sunk in the pit that they made; in the net that they hid, their own foot has been caught.
verses.after: Nations have sunk into the pit they made; their feet are caught in the net they hid.
verses.tsw_comparator: The nations have sunk in the pit that they made; in the net that they hid, their own foot has been caught.

verses.rationale: Retains both unexplained performance terms.
verses.before: The LORD has made himself known; he has executed judgment; the wicked are snared in the work of their own hands. Higgaion. Selah.
verses.after: The LORD has made himself known by executing justice; the wicked are snared by the work of their own hands. Higgaion. Selah
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has made himself known; he has executed judgment; the wicked are snared in the work of their own hands. Higgaion. Selah.

verses.rationale: Preserves directed wish and death-realm term.
verses.before: The wicked will return to Sheol, all the nations that forget God.
verses.after: Let the wicked return to Sheol, all the nations that forget God.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wicked shall return to Sheol, all the nations that forget God.

verses.rationale: Carries negation into parallel line.
verses.before: For the needy will not always be forgotten, and the hope of the poor will not perish forever.
verses.after: For the needy will not be forgotten forever, nor the hope of the poor perish for all time.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the needy shall not always be forgotten, and the hope of the poor shall not perish forever.

verses.rationale: Keeps mortal limitation and universal judgment appeal.
verses.before: Arise, O LORD! Let not man prevail; let the nations be judged before you!
verses.after: Rise, LORD! Do not let mortals prevail. Let nations be judged before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Arise, O LORD! Let not man prevail; let the nations be judged before you!

verses.rationale: Selects fear reading while noting teacher alternative.
verses.before: Put them in fear, O LORD; let the nations know that they are but human. Selah.
verses.after: Strike them with fear, LORD; let the nations know they are only human. Selah
verses.tsw_comparator: Put them in fear, O LORD; let the nations know that they are but human. Selah.

verses.rationale: Retains accusation of distance and concealment.
verses.before: Why, O LORD, do you stand far away? Why do you hide yourself in times of trouble?
verses.after: Why, LORD, do you stand far away? Why do you hide in times of distress?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why, O LORD, do you stand far away? Why do you hide yourself in times of trouble?

verses.rationale: Selects imprecation; victim-entrapment alternative noted.
verses.before: In arrogance the wicked hotly pursue the poor; let them be caught in the schemes that they have devised.
verses.after: In pride the wicked hunt down the poor. Let them be caught in the schemes they devised.
verses.tsw_comparator: In arrogance the wicked hotly pursue the poor; let them be caught in the schemes that they have devised.

verses.rationale: Follows euphemistic curse reading; blessing-greedy alternative noted.
verses.before: For the wicked boasts of the desires of his soul, and the one greedy for gain curses and renounces the LORD.
verses.after: The wicked boast of their cravings; the greedy curse and spurn the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the wicked boasts of the desires of his soul, and the one greedy for gain curses and renounces the LORD.

verses.rationale: Makes inward claims clear without resolving practical/theoretical denial.
verses.before: In the pride of his face the wicked does not seek him; all his thoughts are, “There is no God.”
verses.after: With nose held high, the wicked say, “He will not call us to account.” “There is no God” runs through all their plans.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the pride of his face the wicked does not seek him; all his thoughts are, “There is no God.”

verses.rationale: Retains prosperity’s challenge and contemptuous gesture.
verses.before: His ways prosper at all times; your judgments are on high, out of his sight; as for all his foes, he puffs at them.
verses.after: Their ways prosper at every turn; your judgments are high beyond their sight. They snort at all their enemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: His ways prosper at all times; your judgments are on high, out of his sight; as for all his foes, he puffs at them.

verses.rationale: Keeps boast’s first person within collective description.
verses.before: He says in his heart, “I will not be moved; throughout all generations I will not meet adversity.”
verses.after: They say in their hearts, “I will never be shaken; for generations I will know no trouble.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He says in his heart, “I shall not be moved; throughout all generations I shall not meet adversity.”

verses.rationale: Preserves bodily hiding of harmful speech.
verses.before: His mouth is filled with cursing and deceit and oppression; under his tongue are mischief and iniquity.
verses.after: Their mouths are full of curses, deceit, and oppression; under their tongues lie trouble and wrongdoing.
verses.tsw_comparator: His mouth is filled with cursing and deceit and oppression; under his tongue are mischief and iniquity.

verses.rationale: Keeps actual murder and vulnerable victims.
verses.before: He sits in ambush in the villages; in hiding places he murders the innocent. His eyes stealthily watch for the helpless;
verses.after: They sit in ambush near villages, murdering the innocent in secret. Their eyes watch for the helpless.
verses.tsw_comparator: He sits in ambush in the villages; in hiding places he murders the innocent. His eyes stealthily watch for the helpless;

verses.rationale: Retains repeated poor and mixed lion/net images.
verses.before: he lurks in ambush like a lion in his thicket; he lurks that he may seize the poor; he seizes the poor when he draws him into his net.
verses.after: They lurk in secret like lions in a thicket, waiting to seize the poor; they seize the poor and drag them into their nets.
verses.tsw_comparator: he lurks in ambush like a lion in his thicket; he lurks that he may seize the poor; he seizes the poor when he draws him into his net.

verses.rationale: Selects victim subject in difficult written/read clause.
verses.before: The helpless are crushed, sink down, and fall by his might.
verses.after: The helpless are crushed and sink down; they fall beneath the oppressors’ strength.
verses.tsw_comparator: The helpless are crushed, sink down, and fall by his might.

verses.rationale: Keeps denial of divine attention as quoted claim.
verses.before: He says in his heart, “God has forgotten, he has hidden his face, he will never see it.”
verses.after: The wicked say in their hearts, “God has forgotten; he has hidden his face and will never see.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He says in his heart, “God has forgotten, he has hidden his face, he will never see it.”

verses.rationale: Preserves answering appeal to quoted forgetfulness.
verses.before: Arise, O LORD; O God, lift up your hand; forget not the afflicted.
verses.after: Rise, LORD! God, lift your hand. Do not forget the afflicted.
verses.tsw_comparator: Arise, O LORD; O God, lift up your hand; forget not the afflicted.

verses.rationale: Keeps direct second-person accusation in quoted thought.
verses.before: Why does the wicked renounce God and say in his heart, “You will not call to account”?
verses.after: Why does the wicked person spurn God and say in his heart, “You will not call me to account”?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why does the wicked renounce God and say in his heart, “You will not call to account”?

verses.rationale: Preserves seeing, hand, entrusting, and orphan protection.
verses.before: But you do see, for you note mischief and vexation, that you may take it into your hands; to you the helpless commits himself; you have been the helper of the fatherless.
verses.after: But you do see. You look on trouble and grief to take them into your hands. The helpless leave themselves with you; you have been the orphan’s helper.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you do see, for you note mischief and vexation, that you may take it into your hands; to you the helpless commits himself; you have been the helper of the fatherless.

verses.rationale: Keeps violent power-breaking and complete accounting.
verses.before: Break the arm of the wicked and evildoer; call his wickedness to account till you find none.
verses.after: Break the arm of the wicked and evil person; call his wickedness to account until none remains.
verses.tsw_comparator: Break the arm of the wicked and evildoer; call his wickedness to account till you find none.

verses.rationale: Retains territorial claim and completed destruction.
verses.before: The LORD is king forever and ever; the nations perish from his land.
verses.after: The LORD is King forever and ever; the nations have perished from his land.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD is king forever and ever; the nations perish from his land.

verses.rationale: Keeps heard desire and prepared hearts.
verses.before: O LORD, you hear the desire of the afflicted; you will strengthen their heart; you will incline your ear
verses.after: You have heard the longing of the afflicted, LORD; you strengthen their hearts and incline your ear,
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, you hear the desire of the afflicted; you will strengthen their heart; you will incline your ear

verses.rationale: Preserves human limitation as answer to oppression.
verses.before: to do justice to the fatherless and the oppressed, so that man who is of the earth may strike terror no more.
verses.after: to grant justice to the orphan and the crushed, so that a mortal made of earth may terrify no more.
verses.tsw_comparator: to do justice to the fatherless and the oppressed, so that man who is of the earth may strike terror no more.

verses.rationale: Includes inline source title; retains flight image.
verses.before: In the LORD I take refuge; how can you say to my soul, “Flee like a bird to your mountain,
verses.after: For the director. Of David. In the LORD I take refuge. How can you say to me, “Fly like a bird to your mountain!
verses.tsw_comparator: In the LORD I take refuge; how can you say to my soul, “Flee like a bird to your mountain,

verses.rationale: Keeps concealed attack in quoted warning.
verses.before: for look, the wicked bend the bow; they have fitted their arrow to the string to shoot in the dark at the upright in heart;
verses.after: Look, the wicked bend their bows; they set arrows on the string to shoot from darkness at the upright in heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: for behold, the wicked bend the bow; they have fitted their arrow to the string to shoot in the dark at the upright in heart;

verses.rationale: Retains question and uncertain quotation boundary.
verses.before: if the foundations are destroyed, what can the righteous do?”
verses.after: When the foundations are torn down, what can the righteous do?”
verses.tsw_comparator: if the foundations are destroyed, what can the righteous do?”

verses.rationale: Renders eyelids as gaze while retaining scrutiny.
verses.before: The LORD is in his holy temple; the LORD’s throne is in heaven; his eyes see, his eyelids test the children of humanity.
verses.after: The LORD is in his holy temple; the LORD’s throne is in heaven. His eyes see; his gaze tests humanity.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD is in his holy temple; the LORD’s throne is in heaven; his eyes see, his eyelids test the children of humanity.

verses.rationale: Retains divine hatred’s personal force.
verses.before: The LORD tests the righteous, but his soul hates the wicked and the one who loves violence.
verses.after: The LORD tests the righteous, but his whole being hates the wicked and those who love violence.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD tests the righteous, but his soul hates the wicked and the one who loves violence.

verses.rationale: Follows pinned snares; alternative coals noted.
verses.before: Let him rain coals on the wicked; fire and sulfur and a scorching wind will be the portion of their cup.
verses.after: He rains snares on the wicked; fire, sulfur, and a scorching wind are their cup’s portion.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let him rain coals on the wicked; fire and sulfur and a scorching wind shall be the portion of their cup.

verses.rationale: Keeps seeing-face hope and right conduct.
verses.before: For the LORD is righteous; he loves righteous deeds; the upright will look his face.
verses.after: For the LORD is righteous and loves righteous deeds; the upright will see his face.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD is righteous; he loves righteous deeds; the upright shall behold his face.

verses.rationale: Retains title and communal lament over trust.
verses.before: Save, O LORD, for the faithful have vanished; for the trustworthy have disappeared from among the children of humanity.
verses.after: For the director. According to the Sheminith. A psalm of David. Save us, LORD! The faithful have vanished; the trustworthy have disappeared from humanity.
verses.tsw_comparator: Save, O LORD, for the faithful have vanished; for the trustworthy have disappeared from among the children of humanity.

verses.rationale: Keeps double-heart image with accessible adjective.
verses.before: Everyone utters lies to his neighbor; with flattering lips and a double heart they speak.
verses.after: Everyone lies to a neighbor; they speak with smooth lips and a double heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: Everyone utters lies to his neighbor; with flattering lips and a double heart they speak.

verses.rationale: Preserves bodily imprecation against harmful speech.
verses.before: May the LORD cut off all flattering lips, the tongue that makes great boasts,
verses.after: May the LORD cut off every flattering lip, every tongue that boasts,
verses.tsw_comparator: May the LORD cut off all flattering lips, the tongue that makes great boasts,

verses.rationale: Keeps speech-based claim to unaccountable power.
verses.before: people who say, “With our tongue we will prevail, our lips are with us; who is master over us?”
verses.after: those who say, “With our tongues we will prevail; our lips are our own. Who can rule us?”
verses.tsw_comparator: those who say, “With our tongue we will prevail, our lips are with us; who is master over us?”

verses.rationale: Marks divine answer; difficult final referent noted.
verses.before: “Because the poor are plundered, because the needy groan, I will now arise,” says the LORD; “I will place him in the safety for which he longs.”
verses.after: “Because the poor are plundered and the needy groan, I will now rise,” says the LORD. “I will bring to safety the one who longs for it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Because the poor are plundered, because the needy groan, I will now arise,” says the LORD; “I will place him in the safety for which he longs.”

verses.rationale: Retains metal purity and sevenfold testing.
verses.before: The words of the LORD are pure words, like silver refined in a furnace on the ground, purified seven times.
verses.after: The LORD’s words are pure, like silver refined in an earthen furnace, purified seven times.
verses.tsw_comparator: The words of the LORD are pure words, like silver refined in a furnace on the ground, purified seven times.

verses.rationale: Retains them-to-him shift with individualizing expression.
verses.before: You, O LORD, will keep them; you will guard us from this generation forever.
verses.after: You, LORD, will guard them; you will keep each one safe from this generation forever,
verses.tsw_comparator: You, O LORD, will keep them; you will guard us from this generation forever.

verses.rationale: Keeps continuing surrounding evil after assurance.
verses.before: On every side the wicked prowl, as vileness is exalted among the children of humanity.
verses.after: though the wicked prowl on every side when vileness is exalted among human beings.
verses.tsw_comparator: On every side the wicked prowl, as vileness is exalted among the children of humanity.

verses.rationale: Retains title and repeated open-ended complaint.
verses.before: How long, O LORD? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me?
verses.after: For the director. A psalm of David. How long, LORD? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me?
verses.tsw_comparator: How long, O LORD? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me?

verses.rationale: Keeps inward counsel and repeated how-long structure.
verses.before: How long must I carry counsel in my soul, sorrow in my heart day after day? How long will my enemy be lifted up over me?
verses.after: How long must I wrestle with plans within me, with sorrow in my heart all day? How long will my enemy rise over me?
verses.tsw_comparator: How long must I carry counsel in my soul, sorrow in my heart day after day? How long shall my enemy be lifted up over me?

verses.rationale: Preserves revived sight and death-sleep metaphor.
verses.before: Look upon me; answer me, O LORD my God. Give light to my eyes, so that I do not sleep the sleep of death,
verses.after: Look at me and answer, LORD my God! Give light to my eyes, lest I sleep in death,
verses.tsw_comparator: Look upon me; answer me, O LORD my God. Give light to my eyes, so that I do not sleep the sleep of death,

verses.rationale: Keeps hostile speech and feared triumph.
verses.before: so that my enemy will not say, “I have prevailed,” and my foes do not rejoice because I am shaken.
verses.after: lest my enemy say, “I have overcome him,” and my foes rejoice when I fall.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that my enemy will not say, “I have prevailed,” and my foes do not rejoice because I am shaken.

verses.rationale: Binds first clauses of Hebrew13:6 with exact full-record hash.
verses.before: Yet I have trusted in your steadfast love; my heart will rejoice in your saving help.
verses.after: But I have trusted in your faithful love; my heart will rejoice in your rescue.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I have trusted in your steadfast love; my heart shall rejoice in your saving help.

source_partition.reason: Public Psalm 13:5–6 divides one complete Hebrew record at the clause boundary before אשירה. Full-record hashes include both original numbering notes.

verses.rationale: Binds final clause of same original13:6, documenting split.
verses.before: I will sing to the LORD, because the LORD has dealt bountifully with me.
verses.after: I will sing to the LORD, for he has dealt generously with me.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will sing to the LORD, because the LORD has dealt bountifully with me.

source_partition.reason: Public Psalm 13:5–6 divides one complete Hebrew record at the clause boundary before אשירה. Full-record hashes include both original numbering notes.

verses.rationale: Retains title, inner claim, and moral consequence.
verses.before: The fool says in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt, they do abominable deeds; there is none who does good.
verses.after: For the director. Of David. The fool says in his heart, “There is no God.” They act corruptly and do abhorrent things; no one does good.
verses.tsw_comparator: The fool says in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt, they do abominable deeds; there is none who does good.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine search and paired criteria.
verses.before: The LORD looks down from heaven on the children of humanity, to see if there are any who understand, who seek after God.
verses.after: The LORD looks down from heaven on humanity to see whether anyone understands, whether anyone seeks God.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD looks down from heaven on the children of humanity, to see if there are any who understand, who seek after God.

verses.rationale: Preserves universal rhetoric and emphatic final denial.
verses.before: They have all turned aside; together they have become corrupt; there is none who does good, not even one.
verses.after: All have turned aside; together they have become corrupt. No one does good—not even one.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have all turned aside; together they have become corrupt; there is none who does good, not even one.

verses.rationale: Keeps devouring image and unmarked my-people speaker.
verses.before: Have they no knowledge, all the evildoers who eat up my people as they eat bread and do not call upon the LORD?
verses.after: Do all these evildoers know nothing, devouring my people as they eat bread, never calling on the LORD?
verses.tsw_comparator: Have they no knowledge, all the evildoers who eat up my people as they eat bread and do not call upon the LORD?

verses.rationale: Retains sudden there and divine presence.
verses.before: There they are in great terror, for God is with the generation of the righteous.
verses.after: There they are, terrified, for God is among the righteous generation.
verses.tsw_comparator: There they are in great terror, for God is with the generation of the righteous.

verses.rationale: Keeps direct accusation and refuge contrast.
verses.before: You would shame the plans of the poor, but the LORD is his refuge.
verses.after: You frustrate the poor person’s plans, but the LORD is his refuge.
verses.tsw_comparator: You would shame the plans of the poor, but the LORD is his refuge.

verses.rationale: Preserves wish, restoration idiom, and paired people-names.
verses.before: Oh, that salvation for Israel would come out of Zion! When the LORD restores the fortunes of his people, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad.
verses.after: If only Israel’s rescue would come from Zion! When the LORD restores his people’s fortunes, let Jacob rejoice and Israel be glad.
verses.tsw_comparator: Oh, that salvation for Israel would come out of Zion! When the LORD restores the fortunes of his people, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad.

verses.rationale: Keeps guest/dweller distinction and sacred setting.
verses.before: O LORD, who may dwell in your tent? Who may live on your holy mountain?
verses.after: A psalm of David. LORD, who may be a guest in your tent? Who may dwell on your holy mountain?
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, who may dwell in your tent? Who may live on your holy mountain?

verses.rationale: Makes entry answer natural and conduct-specific.
verses.before: People who walk with integrity, do what is right, and speak truth from the heart;
verses.after: One who walks with integrity, does what is right, and speaks truth from the heart;
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who walk with integrity, do what is right, and speak truth from the heart;

verses.rationale: Keeps three relational speech-and-action refusals.
verses.before: who do not slander with their tongue, do no harm to others, and do not heap shame on their neighbors;
verses.after: who does not slander with the tongue, harm a neighbor, or take up a reproach against a friend;
verses.tsw_comparator: who do not slander with their tongue, do no harm to others, and do not heap shame on their neighbors;

verses.rationale: Selects costly-oath sense while retaining moral discrimination.
verses.before: in whose eyes the contemptible are rejected, but who honor people who fear the LORD; who keep their word even when it costs them;
verses.after: who rejects the contemptible but honors those who revere the LORD; who keeps an oath even when it hurts;
verses.tsw_comparator: in whose eyes the contemptible are rejected, but who honor those who fear the LORD; who keep their word even when it costs them;

verses.rationale: Retains unsoftened interest ban and legal bribery.
verses.before: who do not lend money at interest, and do not take a bribe against the innocent. People who do these things will never be shaken.
verses.after: who does not lend money at interest or take a bribe against the innocent. One who does these things will never be shaken.
verses.tsw_comparator: who do not lend money at interest, and do not take a bribe against the innocent. Those who do these things shall never be shaken.

verses.rationale: Preserves uncertain title and protective appeal.
verses.before: Preserve me, O God, for in you I take refuge.
verses.after: A Miktam of David. Keep me safe, God, for I take refuge in you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Preserve me, O God, for in you I take refuge.

verses.rationale: Reads self-address contextually; grammatical alternative noted.
verses.before: I say to the LORD, “You are my Lord; I have no good apart from you.”
verses.after: I say to the LORD, “You are my Lord; apart from you I have no good.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I say to the LORD, “You are my Lord; I have no good apart from you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps difficult earthly holy-ones referent qualified in note.
verses.before: As for the holy ones in the land, they are the excellent ones, in whom is all my delight.
verses.after: As for the holy ones in the land, they are the noble ones in whom I delight.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the holy ones in the land, they are the excellent ones, in whom is all my delight.

verses.rationale: Retains cultic refusal and uncertain hurry/dowry verb.
verses.before: The sorrows of people who run after another god will multiply; their drink offerings of blood I will not pour out or take their names on my lips.
verses.after: Those who hurry after another god multiply their sorrows. I will not pour out their offerings of blood or take their names on my lips.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sorrows of those who run after another god shall multiply; their drink offerings of blood I will not pour out or take their names on my lips.

verses.rationale: Preserves inheritance, cup, and lot images.
verses.before: The LORD is my chosen portion and my cup; you hold my lot.
verses.after: LORD, you are my allotted portion and my cup; you hold my lot secure.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD is my chosen portion and my cup; you hold my lot.

verses.rationale: Keeps landed allotment metaphor.
verses.before: The lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; indeed, I have a beautiful inheritance.
verses.after: The boundary lines have fallen in pleasant places for me; indeed, my inheritance is beautiful.
verses.tsw_comparator: The lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; indeed, I have a beautiful inheritance.

verses.rationale: Retains ancient inward-organ image with vocabulary aid.
verses.before: I bless the LORD who gives me counsel; in the night also my heart instructs me.
verses.after: I bless the LORD who counsels me; even at night my kidneys instruct me.
verses.tsw_comparator: I bless the LORD who gives me counsel; in the night also my heart instructs me.

verses.rationale: Keeps intentional attention and supporting right hand.
verses.before: I have set the LORD always before me; because he is at my right hand, I will not be shaken.
verses.after: I keep the LORD before me always; with him at my right hand, I will not be shaken.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have set the LORD always before me; because he is at my right hand, I shall not be shaken.

verses.rationale: Preserves glory rather than silently substituting tongue.
verses.before: So my heart is glad, and my whole being rejoices; my flesh also dwells secure.
verses.after: So my heart is glad and my glory rejoices; my flesh too rests securely.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore my heart is glad, and my whole being rejoices; my flesh also dwells secure.

verses.rationale: Follows Hebrew pit; decay possibility noted.
verses.before: For you will not abandon my soul to Sheol, or let your holy one see corruption.
verses.after: For you will not abandon my life to Sheol nor let your faithful one see the pit.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you will not abandon my soul to Sheol, or let your holy one see corruption.

verses.rationale: Keeps path, presence, hand, and lasting joy.
verses.before: You reveal to me the path of life; in your presence there is fullness of joy; at your right hand are pleasures forevermore.
verses.after: You make known to me the path of life. In your presence is fullness of joy; at your right hand are pleasures forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: You make known to me the path of life; in your presence there is fullness of joy; at your right hand are pleasures forevermore.

verses.rationale: Preserves prayer title and claimed honest case.
verses.before: Hear a just cause, O LORD; attend to my cry; give ear to my prayer from lips free of deceit.
verses.after: A prayer of David. Hear a just cause, LORD; attend to my cry. Listen to my prayer from lips without deceit.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear a just cause, O LORD; attend to my cry; give ear to my prayer from lips free of deceit.

verses.rationale: Keeps courtroom appeal and divine sight.
verses.before: From your presence let my judgment come; let your eyes look what is right.
verses.after: Let my vindication come from you; let your eyes see what is right.
verses.tsw_comparator: From your presence let my judgment come; let your eyes behold what is right.

verses.rationale: Selects resolve reading; evil-intent alternative noted.
verses.before: You have tried my heart, you have visited me by night; you have tested me, and you find nothing; I have purposed that my mouth will not transgress.
verses.after: You have tested my heart, visited me by night, refined me and found nothing. I have resolved that my mouth will not transgress.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have tried my heart, you have visited me by night; you have tested me, and you find nothing; I have purposed that my mouth will not transgress.

verses.rationale: Clarifies guarded-path idiom without endorsing violence.
verses.before: As for the works of man, by the word of your lips I have kept myself from the paths of the violent.
verses.after: As for human deeds, by the word of your lips I have kept away from the paths of the violent.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the works of man, by the word of your lips I have kept myself from the paths of the violent.

verses.rationale: Retains sustained foot-and-path imagery.
verses.before: My steps have held fast to your tracks; my feet have not slipped.
verses.after: My steps have held to your tracks; my feet have not slipped.
verses.tsw_comparator: My steps have held fast to your tracks; my feet have not slipped.

verses.rationale: Keeps confident appeal and inclined ear.
verses.before: I call upon you, for you will answer me, O God; incline your ear to me; hear my words.
verses.after: I call to you because you will answer me, God. Turn your ear toward me; hear what I say.
verses.tsw_comparator: I call upon you, for you will answer me, O God; incline your ear to me; hear my words.

verses.rationale: Clarifies refuge and saving-hand relationship.
verses.before: Show your steadfast love in wondrous ways, O Savior of people who take refuge from people who rise up against them at your right hand.
verses.after: Show your wondrous faithful love, you who save by your right hand those who seek refuge from their attackers.
verses.tsw_comparator: Show your steadfast love in wondrous ways, O Savior of those who take refuge from those who rise up against them at your right hand.

verses.rationale: Retains delicate eye and sheltering wings.
verses.before: Keep me as the apple of the eye; hide me in the shadow of your wings
verses.after: Guard me like the pupil of your eye; hide me in the shadow of your wings,
verses.tsw_comparator: Keep me as the apple of the eye; hide me in the shadow of your wings

verses.rationale: Keeps life-threatening encirclement.
verses.before: from the wicked who despoil me, my deadly enemies who surround me.
verses.after: from the wicked who ravage me, from deadly enemies who surround me.
verses.tsw_comparator: from the wicked who despoil me, my deadly enemies who surround me.

verses.rationale: Renders closed fat as insensibility; literal image noted.
verses.before: They close their hearts to pity; with their mouths they speak arrogantly.
verses.after: They close up their unfeeling hearts; their mouths speak arrogantly.
verses.tsw_comparator: They close their hearts to pity; with their mouths they speak arrogantly.

verses.rationale: Follows read us plural and downward threat.
verses.before: They have now surrounded our steps; they set their eyes to cast us down to the ground.
verses.after: They have tracked us and now surround us; they fix their eyes on throwing us to the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have now surrounded our steps; they set their eyes to cast us down to the ground.

verses.rationale: Keeps shift to singular predatory likeness.
verses.before: He is like a lion eager to tear, as a young lion lurking in hiding places.
verses.after: The enemy is like a lion eager to tear, a young lion crouching in hiding.
verses.tsw_comparator: He is like a lion eager to tear, as a young lion lurking in hiding places.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine sword and direct confrontation.
verses.before: Arise, O LORD! Confront him, bring him low; deliver my soul from the wicked by your sword,
verses.after: Rise, LORD! Confront him; bring him down. With your sword, rescue my life from the wicked.
verses.tsw_comparator: Arise, O LORD! Confront him, bring him low; deliver my soul from the wicked by your sword,

verses.rationale: Preserves difficult prosperous-family description with alternatives noted.
verses.before: from men by your hand, O LORD, from men of the world whose portion is in this life. You fill their womb with treasure; they are satisfied with children, and they leave their abundance to their infants.
verses.after: With your hand, LORD, rescue me from mortals, from people of this world whose portion is in this life. You fill their bellies with your stored-up goods; their children have enough, and they leave the rest to their little ones.
verses.tsw_comparator: from men by your hand, O LORD, from men of the world whose portion is in this life. You fill their womb with treasure; they are satisfied with children, and they leave their abundance to their infants.

verses.rationale: Keeps awakening undefined and direct divine likeness.
verses.before: As for me, I will look your face in righteousness; when I awake, I will be satisfied with your likeness.
verses.after: But I will see your face in righteousness; when I awake, I will be satisfied with your likeness.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for me, I shall behold your face in righteousness; when I awake, I shall be satisfied with your likeness.

verses.rationale: Bind the complete historical title and opening confession together; retain Saul separately named.
verses.before: I love you, O LORD, my strength.
verses.after: For the director. Of the LORD’s servant David, who spoke the words of this song to the LORD on the day the LORD rescued him from all his enemies and from Saul. He said: I love you, LORD, my strength.
verses.tsw_comparator: I love you, O LORD, my strength.

verses.rationale: Keep the accumulating defensive images and horn rather than flattening them into abstract security.
verses.before: The LORD is my rock and my fortress and my deliverer, my God, my rock, in whom I take refuge, my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my stronghold.
verses.after: The LORD is my crag, my fortress, my rescuer; my God is my rock, where I take refuge, my shield, the horn of my salvation, my stronghold.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD is my rock and my fortress and my deliverer, my God, my rock, in whom I take refuge, my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my stronghold.

verses.rationale: Connect invocation and rescue without changing praise into a condition of rescue.
verses.before: I call upon the LORD, who is worthy to be praised, and I am saved from my enemies.
verses.after: I call on the LORD, who is worthy of praise, and I am saved from my enemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: I call upon the LORD, who is worthy to be praised, and I am saved from my enemies.

verses.rationale: Preserve entanglement and destructive flood as distinct images.
verses.before: The cords of death encompassed me; the torrents of destruction assailed me;
verses.after: Death’s cords wound around me; torrents of destruction terrified me.
verses.tsw_comparator: The cords of death encompassed me; the torrents of destruction assailed me;

verses.rationale: Retain Sheol and the repeated cords, with traps confronting the speaker.
verses.before: the cords of Sheol entangled me; the snares of death confronted me.
verses.after: Sheol’s cords surrounded me; death’s traps lay ahead of me.
verses.tsw_comparator: the cords of Sheol entangled me; the snares of death confronted me.

verses.rationale: Maintain the movement of the cry toward God and the bodily hearing image.
verses.before: In my distress I called upon the LORD; to my God I cried for help. From his temple he heard my voice, and my cry to him reached his ears.
verses.after: In my distress I called on the LORD; I cried to my God for help. From his temple he heard my voice; my cry came before him, into his ears.
verses.tsw_comparator: In my distress I called upon the LORD; to my God I cried for help. From his temple he heard my voice, and my cry to him reached his ears.

verses.rationale: Preserve repeated shaking and the explicit connection to divine anger.
verses.before: Then the earth reeled and rocked; the foundations also of the mountains trembled and quaked, because he was angry.
verses.after: Then the earth heaved and shook; the mountains’ foundations trembled. They heaved because he was angry.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the earth reeled and rocked; the foundations also of the mountains trembled and quaked, because he was angry.

verses.rationale: Retain the fierce bodily imagery without rationalizing it as merely weather.
verses.before: Smoke went up from his nostrils, and devouring fire from his mouth; glowing coals flamed forth from him.
verses.after: Smoke rose from his nostrils; consuming fire came from his mouth, and blazing coals flared from him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Smoke went up from his nostrils, and devouring fire from his mouth; glowing coals flamed forth from him.

verses.rationale: Keep the heavens bending and God descending as the poem presents them.
verses.before: He bowed the heavens and came down; thick darkness was under his feet.
verses.after: He bent the heavens down and descended, with thick darkness beneath his feet.
verses.tsw_comparator: He bowed the heavens and came down; thick darkness was under his feet.

verses.rationale: Retain cherub as a creature and wind as a winged bearer.
verses.before: He rode on a cherub and flew; he came swiftly on the wings of the wind.
verses.after: He rode a cherub and flew; he soared on the wings of the wind.
verses.tsw_comparator: He rode on a cherub and flew; he came swiftly on the wings of the wind.

verses.rationale: Preserve the enclosing shelter and water-cloud description.
verses.before: He made darkness his covering, his canopy around him, thick clouds dark with water.
verses.after: He made darkness his hiding place, his shelter all around him— dark waters and dense clouds.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made darkness his covering, his canopy around him, thick clouds dark with water.

verses.rationale: Keep the difficult brightness-to-cloud transition and its hail/fire accompaniment.
verses.before: Out of the brightness before him hailstones and coals of fire broke through his clouds.
verses.after: Out of the brightness before him, his clouds swept past, with hail and burning coals.
verses.tsw_comparator: Out of the brightness before him hailstones and coals of fire broke through his clouds.

verses.rationale: Retain the repeated hail and coals in the pinned text rather than assimilating the parallel song.
verses.before: The LORD also thundered in the heavens, and the Most High uttered his voice, hailstones and coals of fire.
verses.after: The LORD thundered in the heavens; the Most High gave his voice— hail and burning coals.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD also thundered in the heavens, and the Most High uttered his voice, hailstones and coals of fire.

verses.rationale: Leave the enemy object implicit as in the poem while retaining arrow/lightning parallelism.
verses.before: And he sent out his arrows and scattered them; he flashed forth lightnings and routed them.
verses.after: He sent his arrows and scattered them; he hurled lightning and threw them into confusion.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he sent out his arrows and scattered them; he flashed forth lightnings and routed them.

verses.rationale: Preserve the shift to direct address and the ancient exposed foundations.
verses.before: Then the channels of the sea were seen, and the foundations of the world were laid bare at your rebuke, O LORD, at the blast of the breath of your nostrils.
verses.after: The channels of water appeared; the foundations of the world lay bare at your rebuke, LORD, at the blast of breath from your nostrils.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the channels of the sea were seen, and the foundations of the world were laid bare at your rebuke, O LORD, at the blast of the breath of your nostrils.

verses.rationale: Use connected action while keeping the rescue-from-water image.
verses.before: He sent from on high, he took me; he drew me out of many waters.
verses.after: He reached down from on high and took hold of me; he drew me out of deep waters.
verses.tsw_comparator: He sent from on high, he took me; he drew me out of many waters.
