verses.rationale: Retain the speaker’s admitted inferiority and the plural haters.
verses.before: He rescued me from my strong enemy and from people who hated me, for they were too mighty for me.
verses.after: He rescued me from my powerful enemy, from those who hated me, for they were too strong for me.
verses.tsw_comparator: He rescued me from my strong enemy and from those who hated me, for they were too mighty for me.

verses.rationale: Keep the hostile encounter and supporting contrast concise.
verses.before: They confronted me in the day of my calamity, but the LORD was my support.
verses.after: They confronted me on the day of my disaster, but the LORD was my support.
verses.tsw_comparator: They confronted me in the day of my calamity, but the LORD was my support.

verses.rationale: Preserve spaciousness as the concrete counterpart of distress.
verses.before: He brought me out into a broad place; he rescued me, because he delighted in me.
verses.after: He brought me out into a broad place; he rescued me because he delighted in me.
verses.tsw_comparator: He brought me out into a broad place; he rescued me, because he delighted in me.

verses.rationale: Retain the speaker’s consequential claim of righteous conduct and bodily metaphor.
verses.before: The LORD dealt with me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands he rewarded me.
verses.after: The LORD dealt with me according to my righteousness; he repaid me according to the cleanness of my hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD dealt with me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands he rewarded me.

verses.rationale: Clarify the relational force of the second clause without weakening wickedness.
verses.before: For I have kept the ways of the LORD, and have not wickedly departed from my God.
verses.after: For I have kept the LORD’s ways; I have not wickedly turned away from my God.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I have kept the ways of the LORD, and have not wickedly departed from my God.

verses.rationale: Preserve the paired nearness and refusal to remove instruction.
verses.before: For all his judgments were before me, and his statutes I did not put away from me.
verses.after: All his judgments were before me; I did not put his statutes away from me.
verses.tsw_comparator: For all his judgments were before me, and his statutes I did not put away from me.

verses.rationale: Keep the first-person integrity claim and personal responsibility.
verses.before: I was blameless before him, and I kept myself from my guilt.
verses.after: I was blameless toward him; I guarded myself against my own wrongdoing.
verses.tsw_comparator: I was blameless before him, and I kept myself from my guilt.

verses.rationale: Retain the deliberate return to verse 20 with the added divine sight.
verses.before: So the LORD has rewarded me according to my righteousness, according to the cleanness of my hands in his sight.
verses.after: So the LORD repaid me according to my righteousness, according to the cleanness of my hands in his sight.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the LORD has rewarded me according to my righteousness, according to the cleanness of my hands in his sight.

verses.rationale: Keep the reciprocal repeated roots rather than substituting unrelated virtues.
verses.before: With the merciful you show yourself merciful; with the blameless man you show yourself blameless;
verses.after: With the faithful you show yourself faithful; with the blameless you show yourself blameless.
verses.tsw_comparator: With the merciful you show yourself merciful; with the blameless man you show yourself blameless;

verses.rationale: Preserve the unsettling last contrast; shrewd conveys the reflexive twisting response.
verses.before: with the pure you show yourself pure; and with the crooked you make yourself seem tortuous.
verses.after: With the pure you show yourself pure, but with the crooked you show yourself shrewd.
verses.tsw_comparator: with the pure you show yourself pure; and with the crooked you make yourself seem tortuous.

verses.rationale: Retain collective affliction and the bodily image of proud eyes.
verses.before: For you save a humble people, but the haughty eyes you bring down.
verses.after: You save an afflicted people, but you bring haughty eyes down.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you save a humble people, but the haughty eyes you bring down.

verses.rationale: Keep the lamp and the shift from direct address to naming God.
verses.before: For it is you who light my lamp; the LORD my God lightens my darkness.
verses.after: You are the one who lights my lamp; the LORD my God brightens my darkness.
verses.tsw_comparator: For it is you who light my lamp; the LORD my God lightens my darkness.

verses.rationale: Retain the military actions and repeated enabling relationship.
verses.before: For by you I can run against a troop, and by my God I can leap over a wall.
verses.after: With you I can charge a troop; with my God I can leap a wall.
verses.tsw_comparator: For by you I can run against a troop, and by my God I can leap over a wall.

verses.rationale: Preserve the tested-metal image and universal refuge invitation.
verses.before: This God—his way is perfect; the word of the LORD proves true; he is a shield for all people who take refuge in him.
verses.after: God’s way is blameless; the LORD’s word has been refined. He is a shield to everyone who takes refuge in him.
verses.tsw_comparator: This God—his way is perfect; the word of the LORD proves true; he is a shield for all those who take refuge in him.

verses.rationale: Keep both exclusive rhetorical questions and the move to our God.
verses.before: For who is God, but the LORD? And who is a rock, except our God?
verses.after: Who is God besides the LORD? Who is a rock except our God?
verses.tsw_comparator: For who is God, but the LORD? And who is a rock, except our God?

verses.rationale: Retain girding as bodily preparation and repeat blameless from verse 30.
verses.before: the God who equipped me with strength and made my way blameless.
verses.after: It is God who belts me with strength and makes my way blameless.
verses.tsw_comparator: the God who equipped me with strength and made my way blameless.

verses.rationale: Keep sure-footed animal imagery and the speaker’s heights.
verses.before: He made my feet like the feet of a deer and set me secure on the heights.
verses.after: He makes my feet like a deer’s and sets me on my heights.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made my feet like the feet of a deer and set me secure on the heights.

verses.rationale: Retain real military skill and the unusual bronze bow image.
verses.before: He trains my hands for war, so that my arms can bend a bow of bronze.
verses.after: He trains my hands for battle; my arms can bend a bronze bow.
verses.tsw_comparator: He trains my hands for war, so that my arms can bend a bow of bronze.

verses.rationale: Keep divine gentleness or condescension as the striking source of greatness; note the lexical question.
verses.before: You have given me the shield of your salvation, and your right hand supported me, and your gentleness made me great.
verses.after: You give me the shield of your salvation; your right hand supports me, and your gentleness makes me great.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have given me the shield of your salvation, and your right hand supported me, and your gentleness made me great.

verses.rationale: Preserve spacious footing and the specific vulnerable joints.
verses.before: You gave a wide place for my steps under me, and my feet did not slip.
verses.after: You give my steps room beneath me, and my ankles do not give way.
verses.tsw_comparator: You gave a wide place for my steps under me, and my feet did not slip.

verses.rationale: Retain the speaker’s relentless violence without recasting enemies as abstract faults.
verses.before: I pursued my enemies and overtook them, and did not turn back till they were consumed.
verses.after: I pursue my enemies and overtake them; I do not turn back until they are finished.
verses.tsw_comparator: I pursued my enemies and overtook them, and did not turn back till they were consumed.

verses.rationale: Keep the explicit physical defeat and inability to stand.
verses.before: I thrust them through, so that they were not able to rise; they fell under my feet.
verses.after: I crush them so they cannot rise; they fall beneath my feet.
verses.tsw_comparator: I thrust them through, so that they were not able to rise; they fell under my feet.

verses.rationale: Repeat girding and preserve the rising/falling opposition.
verses.before: For you equipped me with strength for the battle; you made people who rise against me sink under me.
verses.after: You belt me with strength for battle; you bring those who rise against me down beneath me.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you equipped me with strength for the battle; you made those who rise against me sink under me.

verses.rationale: Render giving the neck as flight while retaining lethal intent.
verses.before: You made my enemies turn their backs to me, and people who hated me I destroyed.
verses.after: You make my enemies turn their backs to me; I destroy those who hate me.
verses.tsw_comparator: You made my enemies turn their backs to me, and those who hated me I destroyed.

verses.rationale: Do not omit the enemies’ appeal to the same LORD or its refusal.
verses.before: They cried for help, but there was none to save; they cried to the LORD, but he did not answer them.
verses.after: They cry for help, but no one saves them; they cry to the LORD, but he does not answer.
verses.tsw_comparator: They cried for help, but there was none to save; they cried to the LORD, but he did not answer them.

verses.rationale: Preserve both degrading images and the pinned pour-out verb.
verses.before: I beat them fine as dust before the wind; I cast them out like the mire of the streets.
verses.after: I grind them like dust before the wind; I pour them out like mud in the streets.
verses.tsw_comparator: I beat them fine as dust before the wind; I cast them out like the mire of the streets.

verses.rationale: Retain internal contention, international rule, and the unknown people.
verses.before: You delivered me from strife with the people; you made me the head of the nations; people whom I had not known served me.
verses.after: You rescue me from the people’s disputes; you make me head of nations. A people I did not know serves me.
verses.tsw_comparator: You delivered me from strife with the people; you made me the head of the nations; people whom I had not known served me.

verses.rationale: Convey feigned or fearful submission without presenting it as free agreement.
verses.before: As soon as they heard of me they obeyed me; foreigners came cringing to me.
verses.after: As soon as they hear of me, they obey; foreigners come cringing before me.
verses.tsw_comparator: As soon as they heard of me they obeyed me; foreigners came cringing to me.

verses.rationale: Preserve withering courage and departure from fortified places.
verses.before: Foreigners lost heart and came trembling out of their fortresses.
verses.after: Foreigners lose heart and come trembling out of their strongholds.
verses.tsw_comparator: Foreigners lost heart and came trembling out of their fortresses.

verses.rationale: Keep the three acclaiming clauses and rock image.
verses.before: The LORD lives, and blessed be my rock, and exalted be the God of my salvation—
verses.after: The LORD lives! Blessed be my rock! Let the God who saves me be exalted!
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD lives, and blessed be my rock, and exalted be the God of my salvation—

verses.rationale: Retain vengeance and subjugation as the speaker’s praise.
verses.before: the God who gave me vengeance and subdued peoples under me,
verses.after: He is the God who gives me vengeance and brings peoples under me.
verses.tsw_comparator: the God who gave me vengeance and subdued peoples under me,

verses.rationale: Keep the third-to-second-person turn and rescue repeated around it.
verses.before: who rescued me from my enemies; yes, you exalted me above people who rose against me; you delivered me from the man of violence.
verses.after: He rescues me from my enemies. Yes, you lift me above those who rise against me; you rescue me from violent men.
verses.tsw_comparator: who rescued me from my enemies; yes, you exalted me above those who rose against me; you delivered me from the man of violence.

verses.rationale: Connect thanksgiving to preceding rescue and preserve its international setting.
verses.before: For this I will praise you, O LORD, among the nations, and sing to your name.
verses.after: That is why I will thank you among the nations, LORD, and sing praise to your name.
verses.tsw_comparator: For this I will praise you, O LORD, among the nations, and sing to your name.

verses.rationale: Follow the read form magnifying victories and retain the explicit Davidic conclusion.
verses.before: Great salvation he brings to his king, and shows steadfast love to his anointed, to David and his offspring forever.
verses.after: He gives his king great victories and shows faithful love to his anointed— to David and his offspring forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Great salvation he brings to his king, and shows steadfast love to his anointed, to David and his offspring forever.

verses.rationale: Bind title with opening verse and keep expanse as the source’s sky image.
verses.before: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of his hands.
verses.after: For the director. A psalm of David. The heavens tell of God’s glory; the expanse announces what his hands have made.
verses.tsw_comparator: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of his hands.

verses.rationale: Preserve the continual personified exchange and overflowing speech.
verses.before: Day to day pours forth speech, and night to night reveals knowledge.
verses.after: Day pours out speech to day; night shares knowledge with night.
verses.tsw_comparator: Day to day pours forth speech, and night to night reveals knowledge.

verses.rationale: Choose the nonverbal-witness reading and note the alternative scope of negation.
verses.before: There is no speech, nor are there words; their voice is not heard—
verses.after: There is no speech, there are no words; their voice is not heard.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is no speech, nor are there words; their voice is not heard—

verses.rationale: Retain pinned line rather than silently replacing with voice; identify the tent’s setting.
verses.before: yet their line goes out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world. In them he has set a tent for the sun,
verses.after: Yet their measuring line goes out through all the earth, their words to the ends of the world. In the heavens he has pitched a tent for the sun.
verses.tsw_comparator: yet their line goes out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world. In them he has set a tent for the sun,

verses.rationale: Preserve masculine sun personification and wedding/athletic images.
verses.before: which comes out like a bridegroom from his chamber, and rejoices like a strong man to run his course.
verses.after: The sun comes out like a bridegroom from his chamber; like a warrior, it rejoices to run its course.
verses.tsw_comparator: which comes out like a bridegroom from his chamber, and rejoices like a strong man to run his course.

verses.rationale: Keep the observable poetic circuit and universal reach of heat.
verses.before: Its rising is from the end of the heavens, and its circuit to the other end of them, and nothing is hidden from its heat.
verses.after: It rises at one end of the heavens and circles to the other; nothing is hidden from its heat.
verses.tsw_comparator: Its rising is from the end of the heavens, and its circuit to the other end of them, and nothing is hidden from its heat.

verses.rationale: Retain two different instruction terms and accessible inexperienced rather than unintelligent.
verses.before: The law of the LORD is perfect, restoring the soul; the testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple;
verses.after: The LORD’s instruction is complete, restoring life; the LORD’s testimony is trustworthy, making the inexperienced wise.
verses.tsw_comparator: The law of the LORD is perfect, restoring the soul; the testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple;

verses.rationale: Preserve matched clauses and bodily effects of instruction.
verses.before: the precepts of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart; the commandment of the LORD is pure, enlightening the eyes;
verses.after: The LORD’s precepts are right, bringing joy to the heart; the LORD’s command is clear, giving light to the eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: the precepts of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart; the commandment of the LORD is pure, enlightening the eyes;

verses.rationale: Do not replace fear with law; retain the distinctive member of the sequence.
verses.before: the fear of the LORD is clean, enduring forever; the judgments of the LORD are true, righteous altogether.
verses.after: Fear of the LORD is pure, enduring forever; the LORD’s judgments are true, altogether righteous.
verses.tsw_comparator: the fear of the LORD is clean, enduring forever; the judgments of the LORD are true, righteous altogether.

verses.rationale: Keep the intensification of both value and sweetness.
verses.before: More to be desired are they than gold, even much fine gold; sweeter also than honey and drippings of the honeycomb.
verses.after: They are more desirable than gold, than much fine gold; sweeter than honey, than honey dripping from the comb.
verses.tsw_comparator: More to be desired are they than gold, even much fine gold; sweeter also than honey and drippings of the honeycomb.

verses.rationale: Preserve warning alongside reward and the turn to direct address.
verses.before: Moreover, by them is your servant warned; in keeping them there is great reward.
verses.after: Your servant is also warned by them; there is great reward in keeping them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moreover, by them is your servant warned; in keeping them there is great reward.

verses.rationale: Connect unknowable errors with the request for acquittal, without limiting them to secret acts.
verses.before: Who can discern errors? Declare me innocent from hidden faults.
verses.after: Who can recognize every error? Clear me of faults hidden from me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who can discern errors? Declare me innocent from hidden faults.

verses.rationale: Take the proud plural as presumptuous acts, noting possible arrogant people, and retain dominion imagery.
verses.before: Keep back your servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not rule over me. Then I will be blameless and innocent of great transgression.
verses.after: Keep your servant back from presumptuous sins too; do not let them rule me. Then I will be blameless, cleared of great transgression.
verses.tsw_comparator: Keep back your servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not rule over me. Then I shall be blameless and innocent of great transgression.

verses.rationale: Keep both spoken and inward expression with the final paired divine images.
verses.before: Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in your sight, O LORD, my rock and my redeemer.
verses.after: May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be welcome before you, LORD, my rock and my redeemer.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in your sight, O LORD, my rock and my redeemer.

verses.rationale: Bind title and prayer, retaining the singular addressee and protective height.
verses.before: May the LORD answer you in the day of trouble! May the name of the God of Jacob protect you!
verses.after: For the director. A psalm of David. May the LORD answer you on a day of distress; may the name of Jacob’s God set you securely on high.
verses.tsw_comparator: May the LORD answer you in the day of trouble! May the name of the God of Jacob protect you!

verses.rationale: Keep the two sacred locations in parallel.
verses.before: May he send you help from the sanctuary and give you support from Zion!
verses.after: May he send you help from the sanctuary and sustain you from Zion.
verses.tsw_comparator: May he send you help from the sanctuary and give you support from Zion!

verses.rationale: Render making fat as favorable acceptance, preserving both offering kinds.
verses.before: May he remember all your offerings and regard with favor your burnt sacrifices! Selah.
verses.after: May he remember all your offerings and accept your burnt offering. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: May he remember all your offerings and regard with favor your burnt sacrifices! Selah.

verses.rationale: Keep the prayer form and paired inward intention.
verses.before: May he grant you your heart’s desire and fulfill all your plans!
verses.after: May he give you your heart’s desire and fulfill all your plans.
verses.tsw_comparator: May he grant you your heart’s desire and fulfill all your plans!

verses.rationale: Retain communal response to the singular king’s deliverance and the banners.
verses.before: May we shout for joy over your salvation, and in the name of our God set up our banners! May the LORD fulfill all your petitions!
verses.after: May we shout for joy at your victory and raise our banners in the name of our God. May the LORD fulfill all your requests.
verses.tsw_comparator: May we shout for joy over your salvation, and in the name of our God set up our banners! May the LORD fulfill all your petitions!

verses.rationale: Mark the singular confession and royal anointing without adding a later identity.
verses.before: Now I know that the LORD saves his anointed; he will answer him from his holy heaven with the saving might of his right hand.
verses.after: Now I know that the LORD saves his anointed; he will answer him from his holy heavens with the saving might of his right hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now I know that the LORD saves his anointed; he will answer him from his holy heaven with the saving might of his right hand.

verses.rationale: Supply the implied first verb modestly and retain the contrast of military resources and invocation.
verses.before: Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we trust in the name of the LORD our God.
verses.after: Some look to chariots, others to horses; we call on the name of the LORD our God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we trust in the name of the LORD our God.

verses.rationale: Preserve the terse opposing movements and collective speakers.
verses.before: They collapse and fall, but we rise and stand upright.
verses.after: They bow down and fall; we rise and stand firm.
verses.tsw_comparator: They collapse and fall, but we rise and stand upright.

verses.rationale: Follow the accented Hebrew pause after save; note the alternative save-the-king reading.
verses.before: O LORD, save the king! May he answer us when we call.
verses.after: LORD, save! May the King answer us when we call.
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, save the king! May he answer us when we call.

verses.rationale: Bind title and royal praise; follow the read rejoicing form without adding new content.
verses.before: LORD, the king rejoices in your strength, and in your salvation how greatly he exults!
verses.after: For the director. A psalm of David. LORD, the king rejoices in your strength; how greatly he celebrates your saving help!
verses.tsw_comparator: LORD, the king rejoices in your strength, and in your salvation how greatly he exults!

verses.rationale: Preserve heart/lips parallelism and the musical marker.
verses.before: The desire of his heart you have given him, and the request of his lips you have not withheld. Selah.
verses.after: You have given him his heart’s desire and have not withheld what his lips requested. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The desire of his heart you have given him, and the request of his lips you have not withheld. Selah.

verses.rationale: Keep God’s initiative and concrete coronation image.
verses.before: You have welcomed him with the blessings of goodness, you set a crown of fine gold on his head.
verses.after: You meet him with blessings of goodness; you place a crown of fine gold on his head.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have welcomed him with the blessings of goodness, you set a crown of fine gold on his head.

verses.rationale: Retain the expansive royal claim without reducing forever to merely long life.
verses.before: He asked you for life, and you gave it to him, length of days forever and ever.
verses.after: He asked you for life, and you gave it— length of days, forever and ever.
verses.tsw_comparator: He asked you for life, and you gave it to him, length of days forever and ever.

verses.rationale: Keep bestowed royal glory as the result of deliverance.
verses.before: His glory is great through your salvation; majesty and splendor you bestow upon him.
verses.after: His glory is great through your saving help; you lay splendor and majesty upon him.
verses.tsw_comparator: His glory is great through your salvation; majesty and splendor you bestow upon him.

verses.rationale: Render plural blessings idiomatically and preserve the joy before God’s face.
verses.before: For you make him most blessed forever; you make him joyful with gladness in your presence.
verses.after: You make him a blessing forever; you gladden him with the joy of your presence.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you make him most blessed forever; you make him joyful with gladness in your presence.

verses.rationale: Retain trust and covenant-like loyalty without importing a formal covenant absent here.
verses.before: Because the king trusts in LORD, and through the steadfast love of the Most High, he will not be shaken.
verses.after: For the king trusts in the LORD; through the Most High’s faithful love he will not be shaken.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because the king trusts in LORD, and through the steadfast love of the Most High, he will not be shaken.

verses.rationale: Preserve direct address without forcing the uncertain king/God addressee.
verses.before: Your hand will find all your enemies; your right hand will find people who hate you.
verses.after: Your hand will find all your enemies; your right hand will find those who hate you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your hand will find all your enemies; your right hand will find those who hate you.

verses.rationale: Retain violent judgment and the shift from you to the LORD.
verses.before: You will make them like a fiery furnace at the time of your appearance. LORD, in his anger, will swallow them up, and fire will devour them.
verses.after: You will make them like a fiery furnace when you appear; the LORD will swallow them in his anger, and fire will consume them.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will make them like a fiery furnace at the time of your appearance. LORD, in his anger, will swallow them up, and fire will devour them.

verses.rationale: Keep the explicit destruction of descendants, with fruit as its parallel image.
verses.before: You will destroy their offspring from the earth, their descendants from among humanity.
verses.after: You will destroy their fruit from the earth, their offspring from the human race.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will destroy their offspring from the earth, their descendants from among humanity.

verses.rationale: Express the adversative relation without weakening hostile intention.
verses.before: Though they plot evil against you, devising schemes, they will not succeed.
verses.after: Though they intend evil against you and devise a plot, they will not succeed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Though they plot evil against you, devising schemes, they will not succeed.

verses.rationale: Preserve the abrupt turn of fleeing enemies and the threat aimed at their faces.
verses.before: For you will put them to flight; you will aim your arrows at their faces.
verses.after: For you will make them turn their backs when you aim your bowstrings at their faces.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you will put them to flight; you will aim your arrows at their faces.

verses.rationale: Return to communal praise and repeat the opening strength theme.
verses.before: Be exalted, LORD, in your strength; we will sing and praise your power.
verses.after: Rise high, LORD, in your strength! We will sing and make music of your might.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be exalted, LORD, in your strength; we will sing and praise your power.

verses.rationale: Preserve the tune-like title and anguished question without explaining abandonment away.
verses.before: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from saving me, from the words of my groaning?
verses.after: For the director. To “The Doe of the Dawn.” A psalm of David. My God, my God, why have you abandoned me? Why are you so far from saving me, from the words of my groaning?
verses.tsw_comparator: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from saving me, from the words of my groaning?

verses.rationale: Retain unrelieved day/night appeal and the speaker’s lack of quiet.
verses.before: O my God, I cry by day, but you do not answer, and by night, but I find no rest.
verses.after: My God, I call by day, but you do not answer; by night too, and I find no rest.
verses.tsw_comparator: O my God, I cry by day, but you do not answer, and by night, but I find no rest.

verses.rationale: Keep the striking enthronement image and note dwelling among as an alternative.
verses.before: Yet you are holy, enthroned on the praises of Israel.
verses.after: Yet you are holy, enthroned on Israel’s praises.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet you are holy, enthroned on the praises of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retain repeated trust and contrast with the speaker’s present experience.
verses.before: In you our ancestors trusted; they trusted, and you delivered them.
verses.after: Our ancestors trusted in you; they trusted, and you rescued them.
verses.tsw_comparator: In you our ancestors trusted; they trusted, and you delivered them.

verses.rationale: Preserve the rescue/shame pairing and repeated remembered confidence.
verses.before: To you they cried and were rescued; in you they trusted and were not put to shame.
verses.after: They cried to you and escaped; they trusted in you and were not put to shame.
verses.tsw_comparator: To you they cried and were rescued; in you they trusted and were not put to shame.

verses.rationale: Keep the dehumanizing self-image as lament, not a narrator’s judgment.
verses.before: Yet I am a worm and not human, scorned by mortals and despised by the people.
verses.after: But I am a worm, not a man, scorned by people and despised by the crowd.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I am a worm and not human, scorned by mortals and despised by the people.

verses.rationale: Make the mocking gestures readable and open their speech.
verses.before: Everyone who see me mock me; they make mouths at me; they shake their heads:
verses.after: Everyone who sees me mocks me; they sneer and shake their heads:
verses.tsw_comparator: All who see me mock me; they make mouths at me; they shake their heads:

verses.rationale: Retain the Hebrew taunt’s second-to-third-person switch and appeal to divine delight.
verses.before: “Trust in the LORD—let the LORD deliver him! Let the LORD rescue him, since the LORD delights in him!”
verses.after: “Commit yourself to the LORD! Let the LORD rescue him; let him save this man, since he delights in him!”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Trust in the LORD—let the LORD deliver him! Let the LORD rescue him, since the LORD delights in him!”

verses.rationale: Keep birth and nursing as concrete foundations of trust.
verses.before: Yet you are the one who took me from the womb; you made me trust at my mother’s breasts.
verses.after: But you brought me out of the womb; you gave me security at my mother’s breasts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet you are the one who took me from the womb; you made me trust at my mother’s breasts.

verses.rationale: Retain the repeated birth image and lifelong relation.
verses.before: On you I was cast from my birth, and from my mother’s womb you have been my God.
verses.after: I was cast upon you from the womb; from my mother’s belly you have been my God.
verses.tsw_comparator: On you I was cast from my birth, and from my mother’s womb you have been my God.

verses.rationale: Preserve the contrast between distant God and nearby distress.
verses.before: Do not be far from me, for trouble is near, and there is no one to help.
verses.after: Do not stay far from me. Trouble is near, and there is no one to help.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not be far from me, for trouble is near, and there is no one to help.

verses.rationale: Keep the animal metaphor and named region rather than substituting human enemies.
verses.before: Many bulls surround me; strong bulls of Bashan encircle me.
verses.after: Many bulls surround me; strong bulls of Bashan close me in.
verses.tsw_comparator: Many bulls surround me; strong bulls of Bashan encircle me.

verses.rationale: Clarify the simile while retaining predatory sound and action.
verses.before: They open wide their mouths at me, like a ravening and roaring lion.
verses.after: They open their mouths against me like a lion tearing prey and roaring.
verses.tsw_comparator: They open wide their mouths at me, like a ravening and roaring lion.

verses.rationale: Preserve the accumulating bodily dissolution images.
verses.before: I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint. My heart is like wax; it is melted within my chest.
verses.after: I am poured out like water; all my bones are pulled apart. My heart has become wax, melting inside me.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint. My heart is like wax; it is melted within my chest.

verses.rationale: Keep strength as the pinned subject and God as the addressed agent of death.
verses.before: My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue sticks to my jaws; you lay me in the dust of death.
verses.after: My strength is dry as a potsherd; my tongue sticks to my jaws. You lay me in the dust of death.
verses.tsw_comparator: My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue sticks to my jaws; you lay me in the dust of death.

verses.rationale: Retain the pinned like-a-lion reading and its broken syntax; note the consequential alternative textual tradition separately.
verses.before: For dogs surround me; a company of evildoers encircles me. They have pierced my hands and my feet—
verses.after: Dogs surround me; a band of evildoers closes in. Like a lion—my hands and feet!
verses.tsw_comparator: For dogs surround me; a company of evildoers encircles me. They have pierced my hands and my feet—

verses.rationale: Preserve emaciation/exposure and the onlookers’ invasive gaze.
verses.before: I can count all my bones— they stare and gloat over me.
verses.after: I can count all my bones; they look on and stare at me.
verses.tsw_comparator: I can count all my bones— they stare and gloat over me.

verses.rationale: Retain both distribution actions without harmonizing later citations.
verses.before: They divide my garments among them, and for my clothing they cast lots.
verses.after: They divide my clothes among themselves and cast lots for my garment.
verses.tsw_comparator: They divide my garments among them, and for my clothing they cast lots.

verses.rationale: Keep direct appeal and the repeated distance motif.
verses.before: But you, O LORD, do not be far away! O my strength, hurry to help me!
verses.after: But you, LORD, do not stay far away! My strength, hurry to help me!
verses.tsw_comparator: But you, O LORD, do not be far away! O my strength, hurry to help me!

verses.rationale: Render the precious only one as the speaker’s irreplaceable life, retaining the dog.
verses.before: Deliver my life from the sword, my only life from the power of the dog.
verses.after: Rescue my life from the sword, my only life from the power of the dog.
verses.tsw_comparator: Deliver my life from the sword, my only life from the power of the dog.

verses.rationale: Preserve the pinned perfect answered and its abrupt turn from petition to assurance.
verses.before: Save me from the mouth of the lion! From the horns of the wild oxen you have answered me.
verses.after: Save me from the lion’s mouth, from the horns of wild oxen— you have answered me!
verses.tsw_comparator: Save me from the mouth of the lion! From the horns of the wild oxen you have answered me.

verses.rationale: Render the communal kin group inclusively without changing the speaker or assembly setting.
verses.before: I will declare your name to my sisters and brothers; among the assembly I will praise you.
verses.after: I will tell my brothers and sisters of your name; in the assembly I will praise you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will declare your name to my sisters and brothers; in the midst of the assembly I will praise you.

verses.rationale: Keep the three calls and both ancestral designations.
verses.before: You who fear the LORD, praise him! All offspring of Jacob, honor him! Stand in awe of him, all offspring of Israel!
verses.after: You who fear the LORD, praise him! All Jacob’s offspring, honor him! All Israel’s offspring, stand in awe of him!
verses.tsw_comparator: You who fear the LORD, praise him! All offspring of Jacob, honor him! Stand in awe of him, all offspring of Israel!

verses.rationale: Retain the reversal of abandonment and the singular afflicted sufferer.
verses.before: For he has not despised or abhorred the affliction of the afflicted; he has not hidden his face from him, but has heard when he cried to him.
verses.after: For he has not despised or recoiled from the afflicted one’s suffering. He has not hidden his face from him; when he cried to him, he heard.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he has not despised or abhorred the affliction of the afflicted; he has not hidden his face from him, but has heard when he cried to him.

verses.rationale: Keep the source of praise and the direct-to-third-person shift.
verses.before: From you comes my praise in the great assembly; I will pay my vows before people who fear him.
verses.after: From you comes my praise in the great assembly; I will fulfill my vows before those who fear him.
verses.tsw_comparator: From you comes my praise in the great assembly; I will pay my vows before those who fear him.

verses.rationale: Retain the shared meal and sudden blessing addressed to participants.
verses.before: The afflicted will eat and be satisfied; people who seek the LORD will praise him. May your hearts live forever!
verses.after: The humble will eat and be satisfied; those who seek the LORD will praise him. May your hearts live forever!
verses.tsw_comparator: The afflicted shall eat and be satisfied; those who seek the LORD shall praise him. May your hearts live forever!

verses.rationale: Preserve the worldwide scope and turn to direct address.
verses.before: All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the LORD; and all the families of the nations will worship before you.
verses.after: All the ends of the earth will remember and return to the LORD; all the families of the nations will bow before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the ends of the earth shall remember and turn to the LORD; and all the families of the nations shall worship before you.

verses.rationale: Keep the reason for universal homage concise.
verses.before: For kingship belongs to the LORD, and the LORD rules over the nations.
verses.after: For kingship belongs to the LORD; he rules over the nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: For kingship belongs to the LORD, and the LORD rules over the nations.

verses.rationale: Take fat ones as prosperous and preserve the difficult final mortal-life clause; note alternatives.
verses.before: All the prosperous of the earth eat and worship; before the LORD will bow everyone who go down to the dust, even people who cannot keep their life.
verses.after: All the prosperous of the earth will eat and bow down; all who go down to the dust will kneel before him, even those who cannot keep themselves alive.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the prosperous of the earth eat and worship; before the LORD shall bow all who go down to the dust, even those who cannot keep their life.

verses.rationale: Preserve generational continuity and Adonai as Lord rather than LORD.
verses.before: Posterity will serve the LORD; future generations will be told of the Lord.
verses.after: Offspring will serve him; the coming generation will be told of the Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: Posterity will serve the LORD; future generations will be told of the Lord.

verses.rationale: Keep the future audience and emphatic completed divine action without specifying an absent object.
verses.before: They will come and proclaim the LORD’s righteousness to a people yet unborn, that the LORD has done it.
verses.after: They will come and tell of his righteousness to a people yet to be born: “He has done it!”
verses.tsw_comparator: They will come and proclaim the LORD’s righteousness to a people yet unborn, that the LORD has done it.

verses.rationale: Keep the title within its source verse and the familiar concrete shepherd image.
verses.before: The LORD is my shepherd; I will not lack.
verses.after: A psalm of David. The LORD is my shepherd; I will lack nothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not lack.

verses.rationale: Preserve resting, pasture, and water as pastoral provisions.
verses.before: The LORD makes me lie down in green pastures; leads me beside still waters;
verses.after: He lets me lie down in green pastures; he leads me beside restful waters.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD makes me lie down in green pastures; leads me beside still waters;

verses.rationale: Keep renewed life and morally/rightly directed paths without severing the shepherd metaphor.
verses.before: restores my life; leads me in paths of righteousness for the sake of the LORD’s name.
verses.after: He restores my life; he guides me along right paths for his name’s sake.
verses.tsw_comparator: restores my life; leads me in paths of righteousness for the sake of the LORD’s name.

verses.rationale: Preserve the turn from he to you and both shepherd’s implements; note death-shadow ambiguity.
verses.before: Even though I walk through the valley of deepest darkness, I fear no evil; for you are with me; your rod and your staff— they comfort me.
verses.after: Even when I walk through a valley of deepest darkness, I will fear no harm, because you are with me. Your rod and your staff give me comfort.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even though I walk through the valley of deepest darkness, I fear no evil; for you are with me; your rod and your staff— they comfort me.

verses.rationale: Keep the host imagery and enemies still present rather than removed.
verses.before: You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies; you anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows.
verses.after: You spread a table before me in the presence of my enemies; you lavish oil on my head; my cup is brimming.
verses.tsw_comparator: You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies; you anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows.

verses.rationale: Follow pointed return and retain pursuing goodness; note dwelling and long-duration alternatives.
verses.before: Surely goodness and steadfast love will pursue me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for length of days.
verses.after: Surely goodness and faithful love will pursue me all my life, and I will return to the LORD’s house for length of days.
verses.tsw_comparator: Surely goodness and steadfast love shall pursue me all the days of my life, and I shall dwell in the house of the LORD for length of days.

verses.rationale: Preserve title and the comprehensive ownership claim including inhabitants.
verses.before: Of David. A psalm. The earth is the LORD’s, and all that fills it, the world and people who dwell in it;
verses.after: Of David. A psalm. The earth belongs to the LORD, with everything in it— the world and all who live in it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Of David. A psalm. The earth is the LORD’s, and all that fills it, the world and those who dwell in it;

verses.rationale: Retain the ancient watery foundations without modernizing the cosmology.
verses.before: for he founded it upon the seas and established it upon the rivers.
verses.after: For he founded it upon the seas and established it upon the rivers.
verses.tsw_comparator: for he founded it upon the seas and established it upon the rivers.

verses.rationale: Keep paired access questions and sacred geography.
verses.before: Who may ascend the mountain of the LORD? And who may stand in his holy place?
verses.after: Who may climb the LORD’s mountain? Who may stand in his holy place?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who may ascend the mountain of the LORD? And who may stand in his holy place?

verses.rationale: Preserve the pinned first-person my life despite its difficulty; note common his life and oath-related interpretations.
verses.before: One with clean hands and a pure heart, who has not lifted up my life to what is empty and has not sworn deceitfully.
verses.after: One with clean hands and a pure heart, who has not lifted up my life to falsehood and has not sworn deceitfully.
verses.tsw_comparator: One with clean hands and a pure heart, who has not lifted up my life to what is empty and has not sworn deceitfully.

verses.rationale: Clarify the answer’s subject and render righteousness in its favorable-judgment sense.
verses.before: Such a one will receive blessing from the LORD, and righteousness from the God of his salvation.
verses.after: Such a person will receive blessing from the LORD and vindication from the God who saves them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Such a one will receive blessing from the LORD, and righteousness from the God of his salvation.

verses.rationale: Follow the plural read form and retain Jacob without silently adding God of; note syntax.
verses.before: This is the generation of people who seek him, who seek your face—Jacob. Selah
verses.after: This is the generation of those who seek him, who seek your face—Jacob. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the generation of those who seek him, who seek your face—Jacob. Selah

verses.rationale: Keep personified entrances and their preparation for the king.
verses.before: Lift up your heads, O gates; be lifted up, O ancient doors, that the King of glory may come in.
verses.after: Lift your heads, you gates! Rise up, you ancient doors, so the King of glory may come in!
verses.tsw_comparator: Lift up your heads, O gates; be lifted up, O ancient doors, that the King of glory may come in.

verses.rationale: Preserve question and martial answer without assigning unsupported speakers.
verses.before: Who is this King of glory? The LORD, strong and mighty, the LORD, mighty in battle.
verses.after: Who is this King of glory? The LORD, strong and mighty, the LORD, mighty in battle.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who is this King of glory? The LORD, strong and mighty, the LORD, mighty in battle.

verses.rationale: Retain the near repetition and slightly changed imperative.
verses.before: Lift up your heads, O gates; lift up, O ancient doors, that the King of glory may come in.
verses.after: Lift your heads, you gates! Lift yourselves up, you ancient doors, so the King of glory may come in!
verses.tsw_comparator: Lift up your heads, O gates; lift up, O ancient doors, that the King of glory may come in.

verses.rationale: Keep the intensified question, hosts title, and closing musical marker.
verses.before: Who is this King of glory? The LORD of Hosts— he is the King of glory. Selah
verses.after: Who is he, this King of glory? The LORD of hosts— he is the King of glory. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who is this King of glory? The LORD of Hosts— he is the King of glory. Selah
